This PR provides PipeWire camera feeds on linuxbsd platform.

The benefits of using PipeWire for camera devices include:

- Not having to use V4L2 kernel API directly. Access to video devices via V4L2 is exclusive (i.e. Other V4L2/PipeWire clients cannot access the webcam while it is already opened with V4L2), using PipeWire for webcam capture allow multiple clients sharing the webcam.
- Better integration with desktop environments. (For example: camera indicator on KDE Plasma)
- Sandboxed camera access is possible by using [XDG Desktop Portal](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal).
- _BSD support_, this one is not confirmed yet, but since PipeWire can run on FreeBSD, it is possible to enable camera feeds support with PipeWire that otherwise requires V4L compatibility to build or run camera module.

Camera feed driver on linuxbsd will be selected at runtime, and fallback to V4L2 driver if failed to initialize PipeWire.

## Vendored PipeWire headers
This PR introduces new thirdparty headers to enable PipeWire support. A brief list of added PipeWire and SPA headers **as of version 1.0.0** (the list may change if we update the headers in future) is documented to give a better grasp on how these headers are included (no pun intended).

 Tested with the following shader:
```gdshader
shader_type canvas_item;

const mat3 yuv2rgb_bt709 = mat3(
	vec3(1.00000, 1.00000, 1.00000),
	vec3(0.00000, -0.21482, 2.12798),
	vec3(1.28033, -0.38059, 0.00000)
);

uniform sampler2D texture_yuy2;

void fragment() {
	vec2 size = TEXTURE_PIXEL_SIZE;
	vec2 UV_u = UV - floor(mod(UV / size, 2)) * vec2(1, 0) * size;
	vec2 UV_v = UV + (vec2(1, 0) - floor(mod(UV / size, 2))) * vec2(1, 0) * size;
	float y = texture(texture_yuy2, UV).r;
	float u = texture(texture_yuy2, UV_u).g;
	float v = texture(texture_yuy2, UV_v).g;
	vec3 rgb = yuv2rgb_bt709 * vec3(y, u - 0.5, v - 0.5);
	COLOR = vec4(rgb, 1.0);
}
```

 Tested with [godot-camerafeed-demo](https://github.com/shiena/godot-camerafeed-demo).
